rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Verify the property and governing jurisdiction
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Research can be wrong if it is done for the wrong property or government office.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Match the property to official records and confirm the city, county, or other agency with zoning authority.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Identifies the correct property and government authority, or explains what still needs confirmation.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Provide the correct zoning district
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Using the wrong district can make every later zoning answer incorrect.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Use the current official zoning map and identify any split zoning, overlay, or boundary issue that could affect the answer.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Names the correct base district and clearly identifies any split zoning, overlay, or map uncertainty.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Provide correct use regulations
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A use can be allowed in different ways, and the required approval path can change the outcome.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: State whether the use is permitted, permitted with conditions, requires a conditional use permit or other approval, is prohibited, or cannot yet be determined. Include related conditions, approval standards, and supporting code sections.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Correctly distinguishes the use status and identifies the applicable conditions, approval path, and any missing facts without guessing.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Classify a use and identify its approval path
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A use may be allowed directly, need special approval, or have extra rules.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Use definitions, use tables, footnotes, overlays, and approval conditions. State when the available facts do not support a firm classification.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Identifies the likely use category, permission status, special rules, and missing facts without guessing.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Provide correct parking regulations
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Parking requirements can vary by use, size, location, existing conditions, and available reductions or alternatives.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Identify the applicable parking requirements, including required spaces, calculation method, accessible parking, loading, bicycle parking, shared or off-site parking, reductions, and approval conditions when applicable. State what property details or municipal confirmation are still needed.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Provides the applicable parking rules and calculation basis, identifies relevant exceptions or alternatives, and clearly separates confirmed requirements from items needing more information.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Provide complete district regulations
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Key rules can be missed if the answer relies only on a use table or short summary.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Include the relevant district rules, including uses, development standards, parking, special rules, and applicable footnotes or cross-references.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Includes all material district rules needed for the request and identifies additional code sections that may affect the answer.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Provide code regulations without losing important exceptions, conditions, or footnotes
rubric_items.why_it_matters: An otherwise correct summary can give the wrong result if it leaves out an exception, condition, footnote, or cross-reference in the code.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Include every material exception, condition, footnote, cross-reference, and limitation that affects the requested regulation. Clearly identify when another code section or municipal confirmation is needed.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Provides the full applicable regulation with all material qualifications and points to the supporting code sections.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Explain nonconforming rules accurately
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Nonconforming rights can depend on the property's history, changes, damage, timing, and permits.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Explain the rules that may apply to continuation, changes, expansion, rebuilding, damage thresholds, and timing. Identify when records or municipal confirmation are needed.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Explains the applicable rules and limits without claiming rights not supported by records or municipal confirmation.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Provide accurate citations
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Citations allow readers to trace important statements to the source material that supports them.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Cite the precise source, page, section, or record that supports each material statement. Do not use a citation that does not substantiate the statement.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Each citation accurately identifies the supporting source and location, and it supports the statement it accompanies.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Provide accurate links to associated code sections
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Direct links let the user verify the exact regulation and its related provisions.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Provide direct, current links to the official code sections that support the response, including related sections when they materially affect the answer.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Every link leads to the relevant official code section and supports the statement it accompanies.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Use the active conversation context in follow-up questions
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Users should not have to repeat details, decisions, or limits already provided.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Use relevant facts and decisions already established in the conversation. Ask a follow-up only when an important detail is unclear, missing, or has changed.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Uses the active conversation context correctly and asks only for information that is truly needed.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Ask one clear question when a request is unclear
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A vague request can lead to the wrong research or analysis.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Ask a short question that resolves the important uncertainty and use known facts where possible.
rubric_items.passing_standard: The question is specific, necessary, and avoids asking for information already provided.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Do not guess an unknown abbreviation
rubric_items.why_it_matters: The same abbreviation can mean different things in different sources.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Use a definition from the source material or ask a focused question.
rubric_items.passing_standard: The meaning is supported by a source or clearly left unresolved.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Clearly separate facts, assumptions, and unknowns
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Readers need to know what is confirmed and what still needs checking.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Label assumptions and missing information next to the affected conclusion.
rubric_items.passing_standard: No assumption is presented as a fact, and important unknowns have a specific next step.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Be honest when a source or tool cannot be reached
rubric_items.why_it_matters: An unsuccessful search must not be described as completed.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Say what could not be reached, retain the verified work, and give the next useful step.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Does not claim to have reviewed an unavailable source and clearly separates completed from incomplete work.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Be honest about what Bassett cannot do
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Users may assume Bassett can access systems or complete actions it cannot.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: State the limitation plainly and give the best practical next step.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Does not claim access, submission, download, or completion without evidence.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Do not treat missing information as a negative answer
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Not finding a record does not prove that the record or approval does not exist.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: State what was searched, what was not found, and which source could confirm the answer.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Does not turn a missing search result into a definite negative finding.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Apply a user correction everywhere it matters
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A correction should change every affected conclusion, not just one sentence.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Update all related statements, conclusions, and next steps that rely on the corrected fact.
rubric_items.passing_standard: No earlier version of the corrected information remains in the result.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Answer every part of a multi-part request
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Missing one part can leave the user without a usable answer.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Track each requested item and answer all of them, or explain why an item cannot be completed.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Every requested item has an answer, status, or clear next step.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Stay within the user's requested scope
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Extra work can add confusion or change work the user did not ask to change.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Complete the requested task and identify optional follow-up work without doing it automatically.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Covers the requested work without unrelated changes.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Keep property facts separate when comparing two properties
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Using facts from the wrong property can make an answer unreliable.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Use only each property's verified details and clearly label shared information.
rubric_items.passing_standard: No address, parcel, approval, or conclusion from one property appears in the other property's result.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Keep research separate from property analysis
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Listing rules is different from deciding how they apply to a property.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: For research, provide current rules and sources without deciding compliance. For analysis, apply rules only to supported property facts.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Clearly states whether the response is research or analysis and does not make a compliance decision when only research was requested.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Give the right next step or CTA when one is needed
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A useful answer should tell the user what to do next when an important fact is missing or a separate review is needed.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: When the answer cannot be completed with available information, give a specific next step, such as a municipal request, needed document, approval, or expert review. Do not add one when no action is needed.
rubric_items.passing_standard: The next step is specific, relevant, and matches the missing information or decision; it is not vague or unnecessary.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Prepare a handoff another person can use
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A vague handoff forces the next reviewer to repeat work.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Summarize the task, verified findings, sources, open items, and next action.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Another reviewer can see what is done, what remains, and what evidence is needed.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Separate zoning rules from other regulated-use requirements
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Some uses also involve state licenses, utility approvals, or other agencies.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Identify the local zoning rules, then separately list outside agency, state, utility, or licensing requirements that need further review.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Clearly separates zoning findings from other requirements and directs unanswered questions to the right agency or expert.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Use the document version the user says is current
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Older documents can give a different answer from the current version.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Use the latest user-designated version and flag any material conflict with an older version.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Relies on the correct version and explains any material conflict.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Handle incomplete or unreadable uploads honestly
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A partial file can create the false impression that the full document was reviewed.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: State what could be read and identify the missing pages or replacement file needed.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Accurately describes the review and does not summarize unseen content.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Use surveys, plans, and municipal records correctly
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Plans and records can be incomplete, outdated, or about a different property.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Check the property match, date, version, approval status, and missing pages. Separate what the record shows from what it does not show.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Uses only supported document facts, identifies the correct record, and notes missing or conflicting materials.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Summarize documents without losing important exceptions, conditions, or footnotes
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A summary can change the meaning if it leaves out an exception, condition, or footnote.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Keep all exceptions, conditions, footnotes, and other limits that could affect the answer.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Keeps every exception, condition, or footnote that could change the decision and points to the source.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Search municipal permit records carefully
rubric_items.why_it_matters: Online permit searches may be incomplete or use a different property identifier.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Search official records using available identifiers, save the source and result details, and separate no result from no record.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Reports the official source, property match, permit details, and any limit or follow-up request needed.

rubric_items.evaluation_criterion: Plan a complete municipal records request
rubric_items.why_it_matters: A request sent to the wrong office or missing key details can delay the report.
rubric_items.expected_behavior: Identify the record type, department, recipient, portal or email, property identifiers, fee or timing information, and special instructions.
rubric_items.passing_standard: Provides a complete, usable request plan and clearly labels information that still needs confirmation.
